notes: Every sha256 below is the blob at public_product_commit. .gitattributes forces eol=lf, so an installed tree's bytes match on every platform.

Population rule: every executable .claude/settings.json.template wires as a hook or statusLine, plus the entry points install.sh names by path (managed runner, its dependency root, managed launcher), the settings template, the post-compact rule, and the system kernel root.
scripts/doctor.sh is excluded: it is the measuring instrument, not a member of the measured population.

daemons/semantic-search/namespace-registry.json pins the product-owned namespace policy artifact. v3 does not attest every semantic-search implementation byte; it pins this policy artifact plus the existing load-bearing population.

FleetBaselineManifest/v5 (aigent-os-2026-08-24-dde2c681) is superseded by this baseline as the current public baseline and remains historical evidence in git history. FleetBaselineManifest/v4 (aigent-os-2026-08-24-a8319faf), v3 (aigent-os-2026-08-23-3bfe7ea3), v2 (aigent-os-2026-08-22-30598546), and v1 (aigent-os-2026-08-19-41051d9e) remain historical evidence further back.

v3 recut reason (program issue #41): daemons/statusline-ctx.sh changed to fix a silent statusline when jq is absent and no delegate is wired (telemetry still wrote, but nothing displayed) — every other hash was recomputed from the same commit and found unchanged.

v4 recut reason (program issue #43): daemons/caddy.sh and daemons/lifecycle-common.mjs changed to add the persisted-text trust-boundary render chokepoint (renderPersisted(), SKILL_CHAINS staleness reporting) -- every other hash was recomputed from the same commit and found unchanged.

v5 recut reason (program issue #43, review R1): daemons/caddy.sh and daemons/lifecycle-common.mjs changed again to fix review findings F1/F2/F4/F5/F7/F8 (quoted trust-tag fields, no fail-open disposition default, canonical render_boundary.py import, future-dated-row handling, max/now validation) -- every other hash was recomputed from the same commit and found unchanged.

v6 recut reason (program issue #43, review R2): daemons/caddy.sh and daemons/lifecycle-common.mjs changed again for review findings N2/N4 (except Exception around the render_boundary import, a stricter now-timestamp shape check). daemons/render_boundary.py is newly added to required_files: daemons/caddy.sh, a pinned UserPromptSubmit hook that fires on every prompt, imports it for its render-safety guarantee, so a tampered or drifted copy of that module must also flip the install NONCOMPLIANT -- every other hash was recomputed from the same commit and found unchanged.
CLAUDE.md, .claude/settings.json and .gitignore are excluded: the installer rewrites them (marker block, placeholder render, managed ignore block), so their installed bytes are never the repo bytes.
.claude/skill-index.json and skills/*/SKILL.md are excluded: caddy-enroll and operator-authored skills legitimately change them, so hashing them would report every customized install as NONCOMPLIANT.

.claude/rules/post-compact-critical.md is excluded: it is operator-owned doctrine (the CLAUDE.md class) -- the installer seeds the starter only into a fresh install and keeps an existing operator file, so its installed bytes are legitimately not the repo bytes.

Operator-owned declarations (program issue #49) change how a required_files hash mismatch is REPORTED, never which paths are pinned or what they hash to. The terminal semantics live in docs/install-security.md, section 'Operator-owned paths'.

daemons/resume-verb.mjs repinned (program issue #49, blocker G1): the resume verb gained the optional declared lifecycle extension step, so its blob changed and the previous hash no longer describes core. Only that one entry moved; every other hash was recomputed and found unchanged. baseline_id and public_product_commit are deliberately NOT recut here, so for this one entry the hash is newer than the commit those labels name.

managed_launcher.scope_note: v1 attests the launcher files in the tree only. The PATH shim and desktop/Start-menu shortcuts that launcher/install.* create land outside the install root and are out of scope for a read-only in-tree attestation.

auto_refresh.note: kill_switch_file is resolved under the first existing kill_switch_roots entry, mirroring memRoot() in daemons/lifecycle-common.mjs. When expected is enabled, an active kill switch or an unloadable node-pty is NONCOMPLIANT.
